findings.reason: The diff removes the early `return comp` in replaceXRange. At head, range.js:418-424 maps any range with a wildcard major (e.g. 'x.1.2') to '*', and range.js:462-463 maps '1.x.3' to '>=1.0.0 <2.0.0-0', dropping the patch. Before, the unchanged comp failed the Comparator parse at range.js:157 (or the loose filter at :148). The trigger is traced: satisfies('9.0.0','x.1.2') now returns true.
findings.claim: Removing the invalidXRangeOrder guard makes malformed X-ranges like x.1.2 or 1.x.3 parse as wide ranges, where before they were rejected.
findings.evidence: The diff removes `if (invalidXRangeOrder(M, m, p)) { return comp }` from replaceXRange, along with the helper `(isX(M) && !isX(m)) || (isX(m) && p && !isX(p))`. In the code at head, `x.1.2` has xM true, so it reaches `ret = '*'` at line 424 ("nothing is forbidden"), and `1.x.3` has xm true, so it reaches `ret = `>=${M}.0.0${pr} <${+M + 1}.0.0-0`` at line 463, which drops the stated patch. Before the change the comp came back unchanged, failed the Comparator regex in parseRange (line 157; in loose mode it was filtered out at line 148) and was treated as invalid. Nothing else in parseRange checks the order of X components, so no other guard does this job now. I found no test that pins the old rejection: grep of test/ finds no `x.1`, `*.1` or `1.x.2` cases.
